commons.title: Brooklyn Museum 74.66.5 Shoulder Headdress Zigiren-wunde (3).jpg
commons.description: This headdress is known as zigiren-wunde, or “the new bride.” Entirely secular in nature, it celebrates the role of Baga women in both human and agricultural fertility, and in nurturing the community.    The zigiren-wunde is owned and performed by groups of young men solely for entertainment, especially at weddings. The performer wears it on top of the head, grasping the leglike projections at the base of the mask to steady it. These “shoulders” are draped with cloth, leaving the figure's breasts exposed, and the costume is completed with the addition of a skirt of palm fiber.
commons.editorial_reason: The image shows a headdress, but its description explicitly attributes the tradition to Baga people rather than Landuma.
